title: Smooth points of the stack of curves detected by unobstructed deformations
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Assume $\mathcal C$ is algebraic: it has representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Smoothness of scheme charts is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There exists a largest open substack $\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal C$ smooth over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. For every field $k$ [def-weil-field] there exists a coefficient ring $\Lambda$ with residue field $k$ of the following form: if $\operatorname{char}k=0$, take $\Lambda=k$; if $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, take a Cohen ring with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. A local ring here is a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring is one whose ideals satisfy the descending chain condition. For a Noetherian local ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with specified residue field $k$, let $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$ be the category of Artinian local $\Lambda$-algebras $A$ with a specified identification $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$, and local $\Lambda$-homomorphisms inducing the identity on $k$. A deformation of a $k$-scheme $X$ over $A$ is a flat scheme $X_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ with an identification $X_A\times_A k\cong X$; arrows are isomorphisms compatible with these identifications. The deformation category $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$ is unobstructed if, for every surjection $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$ and every deformation $X_A$, there is a flat deformation $X_{A^\prime}$ and an isomorphism $X_{A^\prime}\times_{A^\prime}A\cong X_A$ compatible with the identified special fibres. For every proper $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension at most one and every coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of the indicated form, its classifying point $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal C$ factors through $\mathcal M$ if and only if $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$ is unobstructed. An open substack means one whose pullback along any scheme-valued object is an open subscheme; smoothness over Z means the composite of a smooth scheme atlas with the structure morphism is smooth. Empty and disconnected schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DZU (lemma-in-smooth-locus), including the Cohen-ring choice in the preceding paragraph; existence of the smooth open is stacks-morphisms.tex lemma-where-smooth as invoked there. The statement concerns every proper curve, without an lci or isolated-singularity assumption.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-maximal-smooth-open] to $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, giving the largest smooth open $\mathcal M$. The existing curve limit theorem [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation] and [lem-sfb-stack-limit-preserving-lfp] show that this morphism is locally of finite presentation. These general statements concern algebraic stacks, which include effective etale descent for objects and the sheaf property for isomorphisms. The item assumes only the representable diagonal and the smooth surjective scheme atlas; [lem-sfb-curve-descent-isom-spaces] shows that $\mathcal C$ is an fppf stack, hence an etale stack since etale coverings are fppf coverings. With the assumed diagonal and atlas, $\mathcal C$ is an algebraic stack, which is the hypothesis of both general statements.

source.place: Tag 0DZU, lemma-in-smooth-locus, first paragraph (maximal open and local finite presentation)

proof.text: In characteristic zero choose $\Lambda=k$. In characteristic $p>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist] supplies a Cohen ring with identified residue field $k$. Fix any allowed $\Lambda$, not just the one chosen. It is Noetherian: a field has only two ideals and a Cohen ring is a principal ideal domain by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. It is torsion-free over $\mathbf Z$: in the mixed-characteristic case it is a domain with nonzero uniformizer $p$; every prime other than $p$ has nonzero residue and is a unit, so every nonzero integer acts injectively. The characteristic-zero field case is immediate. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] with the PID $\mathbf Z$ shows that $\Lambda$ is flat over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tag 0DZU, lemma-in-smooth-locus, preceding Cohen-ring choice and first paragraph (flat coefficient base)

proof.text: Fix $A\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$ for some $N$. Let $Y/A$ be a flat scheme deformation with marked fibre $X$. Since $X/k$ is proper, it is locally of finite type, and [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] over the field $k$ makes it locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-nilpotent-base-change-reflection] with $I=\mathfrak m_A$ to obtain properness of $Y/A$, and [lem-sfb-flat-deformation-lfp] to obtain local finite presentation. Properness supplies quasi-compactness and a closed-immersion diagonal. A closed immersion is affine and therefore quasi-compact, so the diagonal is quasi-compact. Thus $Y/A$ is quasi-separated as well as quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, which is exactly finite presentation. Every geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ factors through $k$, since its map to a field kills the nilpotent maximal ideal. Its fibre is therefore the corresponding geometric fibre of the marked $X/k$. On each affine open of $X$, [lem-pc-dim-base-change] preserves dimension after every field extension, so this geometric fibre has dimension at most one; the base changes of these affine opens cover it. Thus $Y/A$ is an object of $\mathcal C(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0DZU, lemma-in-smooth-locus, last paragraph (flat scheme deformations have all curve-family properties)

proof.text: Conversely, a marked object $Y/A$ of the curve stack has special fibre isomorphic to the scheme $X$. Its special-fibre inclusion $X\hookrightarrow Y$ is a thickening: on an etale affine chart its ideal is generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_A$, whose $N$th power vanishes. A quotient by a nilpotent ideal has exactly the same prime ideals, with the same topology. Thus [lem-sfb-thickening-of-scheme-space] shows that $Y$ is a scheme. Together with step 3 this identifies the marked object groupoids in the two definitions. Their arrows are exactly the same $A$-isomorphisms respecting the same special-fibre marking. For a local map $A\to B$ in the coefficient category, both pullbacks are $Y\times_A B$ with the marking induced by $Y\times_A k\cong X$. The same formula sends a marked isomorphism to its base change. Consequently the comparison commutes with restriction on objects and arrows, including the given isomorphism to an object over $A$ when lifting across $A^\prime\twoheadrightarrow A$. Hence the identification is an equivalence over $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,k}$, respecting restriction along every surjection; in particular it preserves and reflects unobstructedness.

source.place: Tag 0DZU, lemma-in-smooth-locus, comparison paragraph (scheme versus algebraic-space deformation groupoids)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C_\Lambda=\mathcal C\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$, and let $x_0$ denote $X$ over its residue point. This stack is algebraic. It is a stack since $\mathcal C$ is one [lem-sfb-curve-descent-isom-spaces]: triples $(\xi,t,\beta)$ descend componentwise, $\beta$ by the sheaf property of isomorphisms. For the atlas, choose the assumed representable smooth surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal C$. Its pullback has scheme source $U_\Lambda=U\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ and is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Surjectivity uses the current statement's field-extension local lifting convention, which agrees with its chart test for this representable atlas. Its diagonal is the pullback of the original space-representable diagonal: two objects over a test scheme have the same isomorphism space with their fixed maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$. Thus the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. The structural map $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1. Hence [lem-sfb-stack-maximal-smooth-open], using precisely its flat-base-change clause and the flatness of $\Lambda/\mathbf Z$ in step 2, shows that the largest smooth open of $\mathcal C_\Lambda$ is $\mathcal M_\Lambda=\mathcal M\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$. Thus $x$ factors through $\mathcal M$ exactly when $x_0$ factors through $\mathcal M_\Lambda$: both tests pull back the same open to the same $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Also $\mathcal C_\Lambda$ satisfies the limit condition: on every affine $\Lambda$-scheme its groupoid is $\mathcal C(T)$, and [lem-sfb-curve-limit-preservation] applies to the underlying inverse system. By [lem-sfb-stack-limit-preserving-lfp] it is locally finitely presented over $\Lambda$, hence locally of finite type (a finite presentation has finitely many algebra generators).

source.place: Tag 0DZU, lemma-in-smooth-locus, first paragraph (flat base change and the residue point)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-artinian-smoothness-criterion] with $R=\Lambda$, $\mathcal X=\mathcal C_\Lambda$, and $x_0$. Step 2 supplies a Noetherian local base with residue field $k$, and step 5 supplies local finite type and algebraicity. The residue map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ is a finite type closed immersion, so the finite-type residue-point hypothesis of the source criterion holds even when $k$ is not finitely generated over its prime field. The criterion says that $x_0$ belongs to $\mathcal M_\Lambda$ exactly when its marked Artinian deformation groupoid has lifts over every surjection. Step 4 identifies these lifts, including their compatible special-fibre markings, with those defining $\operatorname{Def}_{X,\Lambda}$. Step 5 identifies the left condition with the original factorization through $\mathcal M$. This proves the claimed equivalence for every allowed $\Lambda$.
